draft.title: The nuclear arms race
card: The United States used atomic bombs in 1945. The Soviet Union tested its own bomb in 1949. Each side then built more and better nuclear weapons, so that neither would fall behind.
Both sides came to hold enough weapons to destroy the other. This meant a nuclear attack risked a devastating reply, which is one reason the superpowers avoided direct war.

In 1962 the Soviet Union placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, close to the United States. The United States blockaded Cuba and demanded their removal. After days of tension, the Soviet Union agreed to withdraw the missiles.
The crisis showed how close the world had come to nuclear war. Afterwards, the two sides set up a direct communication link and agreed to treaties that limited some tests and weapons.
draft.remember: Each side built weapons to match the other, and the 1962 crisis showed the danger and pushed both to limit arms.

a.q: Why did the superpowers keep building nuclear weapons after 1949?
opts: Each feared falling behind the other
Each wanted to use them against smaller states
Treaties required both to build more
Each wanted to prove their weapons were safe
a.why: Each side built weapons to keep up with the other, so a rise on one side led to a rise on the other. The weapons were not built for use against small states, and no treaty required the build-up.
a.clue: Think about how each side reacted to the other's weapons.

b.q: What was the main effect of the Cuban Missile Crisis on relations between the superpowers?
opts: It showed the danger of war and led to arms control steps
It ended the rivalry between the two superpowers
It led the United States to invade Cuba
It led the Soviet Union to stop building weapons
b.why: The crisis brought the superpowers close to nuclear war, so both took steps such as a direct communication link and limits on testing. The rivalry did not end, and both kept building weapons.
b.clue: Think about what both sides did once they saw how close war had come.

a.best: Each feared falling behind the other

b.best: It showed the danger of war and led to arms control steps
